statement: An estimated 1.095 billion people were living with a mental disorder globally in 2021.
source_titles: World mental health today: latest data;Mental disorders
locator: World mental health today, Table 2.1; WHO Mental disorders fact sheet, opening epidemiology section
definition: Point prevalence of GBD 2021 mental-disorder categories, adjusted for independent comorbidity but not dependent comorbidity.
method_note: Modeled estimate, not a count of diagnosed people. WHO rounds this to 1.1 billion / nearly one in seven in public-facing text.
license_note: Use as an attributed numeric claim; do not imply the underlying microdata are WHO-owned or freely redistributable.

statement: The age-standardized prevalence of mental disorders was estimated at 13.6% globally in 2021.
source_titles: World mental health today: latest data
locator: Table 2.1
definition: Age-standardized prevalence across the GBD 2021 mental-disorder aggregate.
method_note: Use for global scale, not as a simple national wellbeing ranking metric.

statement: Anxiety disorders affected an estimated 359 million people globally in 2021.
source_titles: World mental health today: latest data
locator: Table 2.1
definition: WHO table notes that the GBD anxiety category includes anxiety disorders and PTSD.
method_note: Modeled prevalence estimate.

statement: Depressive disorders affected an estimated 332 million people globally in 2021.
source_titles: World mental health today: latest data
locator: Table 2.1
definition: WHO table includes major depressive disorder and dysthymia in depressive disorders.
method_note: Modeled prevalence estimate.

statement: Mental disorders accounted for an estimated 155 million DALYs globally in 2021.
source_titles: Global Health Metrics: Mental disorders—Level 2 cause (GBD 2021)
locator: GBD 2021 Mental disorders Level 2 cause summary, opening summary
definition: Disability-adjusted life years attributable to the GBD mental-disorders Level 2 cause.
method_note: 95% uncertainty interval 117–198 million; the source says YLDs contributed to almost all mental-disorder DALYs.
license_note: Use as an attributed result under applicable IHME terms.

statement: Mental disorders accounted for about 5.4% of global DALYs in 2021.
source_titles: Global Health Metrics: Mental disorders—Level 2 cause (GBD 2021)
locator: GBD 2021 Mental disorders Level 2 cause summary, opening summary
definition: Share of all-cause DALYs attributed to mental disorders in GBD 2021.
method_note: 95% uncertainty interval 4.3–6.5%.
license_note: Use as an attributed result under applicable IHME terms.

statement: The global median share of total government health expenditure allocated to mental health was 2.1% among reporting countries.
source_titles: Mental Health Atlas 2024
locator: Executive summary, p. 3; financing and workforce
definition: Median percentage of total government health expenditure allocated to mental health among countries supplying relevant expenditure data.
method_note: The report states this was unchanged from the 2017 and 2020 Atlas estimates; response completeness varies by indicator.
license_note: WHO CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO conditions apply to the report.

statement: The global median government mental-health expenditure was US$2.69 per person among reporting countries.
source_titles: Mental Health Atlas 2024
locator: Executive summary, p. 3; financing and workforce
definition: Government mental-health expenditure per capita among reporting countries.
method_note: Income-group medians differ dramatically; use this global median only with distribution context.
license_note: WHO CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO conditions apply to the report.

statement: Low-income countries reported a median government mental-health expenditure of about US$0.04 per person.
population: Reporting countries in the World Bank low-income group
source_titles: Mental Health Atlas 2024
locator: Executive summary, p. 3; financing and workforce
definition: Income-group median government mental-health expenditure per capita.
method_note: Survey response coverage differs across indicators and countries.
license_note: WHO CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO conditions apply to the report.

statement: High-income countries reported a median government mental-health expenditure of US$65.89 per person.
population: Reporting countries in the World Bank high-income group
source_titles: Mental Health Atlas 2024
locator: Executive summary, p. 3; financing and workforce
definition: Income-group median government mental-health expenditure per capita.
method_note: Survey response coverage differs across indicators and countries.
license_note: WHO CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO conditions apply to the report.

statement: The global median specialized mental-health workforce was 13.5 workers per 100,000 people.
source_titles: Mental Health Atlas 2024;WHO Global Health Observatory — mental health service availability: human resources
locator: Mental Health Atlas 2024 executive summary, p. 3; WHO GHO human-resources indicator group
definition: Specialized mental-health workers per 100,000 population.
method_note: Use Atlas 2024 for the survey-cycle global median and GHO/country profiles for country-level observations.

statement: The Atlas reports only about 1.1–2.4 specialized mental-health workers per 100,000 people in low- and lower-middle-income country groups.
unit: workers per 100,000 population (upper end of reported income-group range)
source_titles: Mental Health Atlas 2024
locator: Executive summary, p. 3; financing and workforce
definition: Income-group medians/range for specialized mental-health workers per 100,000 population.
method_note: The report presents the low-income and lower-middle-income values as a 1.1–2.4 range in its summary; retain the range rather than collapsing it to one point estimate.

statement: High-income countries reported a median 67.2 specialized mental-health workers per 100,000 people.
source_titles: Mental Health Atlas 2024
locator: Executive summary, p. 3; financing and workforce
definition: Income-group median specialized mental-health workforce per 100,000 population.
method_note: Compare with low-income groups only as a health-system capacity indicator, not as a direct measure of care quality.

statement: Fewer than 10% of responding countries had fully moved from institutional models to community-based mental-health care.
source_titles: Mental Health Atlas 2024
locator: Executive summary, p. 3; mental health services
definition: Countries assessed as fully transitioned from institutional-based to community-based service models.
method_note: The source reports an inequality, not an exact percentage; retain 'fewer than 10%' in prose.

statement: 52.9% of responding countries remained in an early stage of transition toward community-based mental-health care.
source_titles: Mental Health Atlas 2024
locator: Executive summary, p. 3; mental health services
definition: Countries classified in the Atlas as remaining in an early stage of service transition.
method_note: A systems-reform indicator, not a patient-level outcome.

statement: Psychosis service coverage was estimated at about 40% in the small set of countries with sufficiently complete data.
population: People with psychosis in 22 countries with sufficient data
source_titles: Mental Health Atlas 2024
locator: Table 34 / executive summary service coverage section
definition: Estimated proportion of people with psychosis who received services, derived from treated prevalence divided by estimated psychosis prevalence.
method_note: The Atlas explicitly says the estimate is indicative rather than definitive because only 22 countries provided sufficient data. Table 34 gives mean 41% and median 40%; use 40% as the report's summary figure.

statement: A WHO fact sheet states that only 29% of people with psychosis receive formal mental-health care, citing Mental Health Atlas 2020.
source_titles: Mental disorders
locator: Health systems and social support section
definition: Formal mental-health care coverage for people with psychosis as summarized by WHO using Atlas 2020 evidence.
method_note: Do not present this as a directly comparable predecessor to the Atlas 2024 40% estimate; coverage definitions, source years and country samples differ.

statement: Modeled mental-health service use for major depressive disorder was 33% in high-income locations.
period: Studies with data from 2000–2019; review published 2022
population: People meeting study criteria for major depressive disorder
source_titles: The global gap in treatment coverage for major depressive disorder in 84 countries from 2000–2019: A systematic review and Bayesian meta-regression analysis
locator: Abstract / Author summary; predicted treatment rates by income group
definition: Estimated proportion of MDD cases using mental-health services.
method_note: Bayesian meta-regression; 95% uncertainty interval 8–66%.

statement: Modeled mental-health service use for major depressive disorder was 8% in low- and lower-middle-income locations.
period: Studies with data from 2000–2019; review published 2022
population: People meeting study criteria for major depressive disorder
source_titles: The global gap in treatment coverage for major depressive disorder in 84 countries from 2000–2019: A systematic review and Bayesian meta-regression analysis
locator: Abstract / Author summary; predicted treatment rates by income group
definition: Estimated proportion of MDD cases using mental-health services.
method_note: Bayesian meta-regression; lower 95% uncertainty bound was reported as <1%, upper bound 36%. Sparse low-resource data are a major limitation.

statement: Minimally adequate treatment for major depressive disorder was estimated at 23% in high-income locations.
period: Studies with data from 2000–2019; review published 2022
population: People meeting study criteria for major depressive disorder
source_titles: The global gap in treatment coverage for major depressive disorder in 84 countries from 2000–2019: A systematic review and Bayesian meta-regression analysis
locator: Abstract / Author summary
definition: Modeled share of MDD cases receiving minimally adequate treatment under the review's harmonized definitions.
method_note: 95% uncertainty interval 2–55%; definitions of minimally adequate treatment vary and were harmonized by the review.

statement: Minimally adequate treatment for major depressive disorder was estimated at 3% in low- and lower-middle-income locations.
period: Studies with data from 2000–2019; review published 2022
population: People meeting study criteria for major depressive disorder
source_titles: The global gap in treatment coverage for major depressive disorder in 84 countries from 2000–2019: A systematic review and Bayesian meta-regression analysis
locator: Abstract / Author summary
definition: Modeled share of MDD cases receiving minimally adequate treatment under the review's harmonized definitions.
method_note: Lower 95% uncertainty bound was reported as <1%, upper bound 25%; low-resource evidence is sparse.

statement: An estimated 12 billion productive work days are lost each year to depression and anxiety.
period: Annual estimate cited in WHO 2025 report
population: Working-age population; underlying study covered 36 countries representing about 80% of global population
source_titles: World mental health today: latest data
locator: Chapter 3, economic consequences, p. 29
definition: Productive work days lost through absenteeism, presenteeism and staff turnover associated with depression and anxiety.
method_note: WHO 2025 report cites a 2016 economic analysis; use as an economic framing estimate, not a current administrative count.
license_note: WHO reuse terms apply; cite the underlying study when used prominently.

statement: The same analysis estimated nearly US$1 trillion per year in productivity losses from depression and anxiety.
period: Annual estimate cited in WHO 2025 report
population: Working-age population; underlying study covered 36 countries representing about 80% of global population
source_titles: World mental health today: latest data
locator: Chapter 3, economic consequences, p. 29
definition: Estimated productivity cost associated with depression and anxiety.
method_note: Based on a 2016 analysis cited by WHO; useful for scale but not a contemporaneous 2025 accounting estimate.
license_note: WHO reuse terms apply; cite the underlying study when used prominently.
